Cotton Sweatshirts were first used as athletic garments in the 1920s and 30s and always featured full length ribknit cuffs and hems, and V-shaped inserts in the neckline. The Wythe Sweatshirt stays true to these details, and adds a subtle curve into the V insert (lovingly called "Doritos" by some vintage aficionados) that gracefully matches the curve of the neckline.
Our crewneck sweatshirt has been a Wythe staple from the very beginning and was one of our earliest products. While we really loved the slimmer, athletic fit of our original sweatshirts, we figured we'd listen to the overwhelming majority of feedback. This new sweatshirt fit features a tighter neckline, roomier sleeves, and removed shoulder seams.
The early inspiration for the FW25 collection was "what astronomers might wear stargazing or watching comets fly by" due to getting caught up in some amazing books about astronomers in the 16th centuries. These books had beautiful paintings of comets and we ran with it. The Comet Kings are a fictional team we came up with through the development process.
• 100% long staple BCIS certified cotton yarns
• Fleece interior for the perfect softness you want in a sweatshirt

This collaboration brings together two family-run brands with more than a century of history behind each of them. Founded in 1911 and 1920 respectively, Merz b. Schwanen and Dehen share a deep commitment to preserving traditional apparel manufacturing, relying on skilled hands while maintaining methods that have increasingly disappeared from modern apparel production.
Designed in collaboration with Merz b. Schwanen and made in Portland by Dehen 1920, this collaborative Pilot Jacket draws from classic flight jackets and traditional workwear. Its Black shell is cut from a durable 12 oz. dry waxed cotton by Halley Stevensons, who have been producing waxed cotton in Scotland since 1864. Water-resistant, hard-wearing, and designed to develop a rich patina with time and use, the fabric brings another long tradition of manufacturing and craftsmanship to the project.

A homage to the service shirts worn by US Armed Forces during WW2, this lightweight yet tough shirt combines a vintage military silhouette with a hardwearing 8oz Japanese Oxford cloth. Woven with double warp and double weft yarns, the fabric displays a slightly more irregular, subtly slubby texture, with a little more heft compared to other plain weaves at the same weight. To complement the 1940s-style cut, we’ve used sulphur-dyed yarns, allowing the fabric to mellow and fade, developing with timeworn character as the shirt ages.
As a military cut, the fit is a little roomier and more relaxed compared to our traditional work shirt, with larger flap-down chest pockets and button fastenings throughout. Seen here in authentic army green, with tonal buttons and red internal bobbin thread for a splash of colour.
